title: Where can two lines disagree?
hook: Update two candidate slopes with explicit likelihoods.

doesNotKnow: Slopes 0/1 have equal priors. Observing y=1 at x=1 has likelihoods .2/.8. Which slope gains weight?

objective: Compute the bayesian posterior lines finite model and explain its changed countercase and stated boundary.

claims.text:
1. bayesian-posterior-lines

Target / packet: ai-bayesian-posterior-lines · P1. Prerequisites: ai:linear-regression-fit, probability:bayesian-updating.

Nearest / distinct payoff: linear-regression-fit → outlier-flattens-line. Existing line fitting returns one estimate; this maintains explicit posterior mass over two line hypotheses and transfers it to location-dependent predictive spread.

Finite primary model: Finite slope hypotheses 0,1, intercept 0 and equal priors. Observation(x=1, y=1) has declared likelihoods [.2,.8], giving posterior [.2,.8]. At x=2 predictions[0,2], mean 1.6, variance=.64; at x=0 both predict 0 with variance 0.

Countercase and mathematical boundary: Observation y=0 has likelihoods [.8,.2], reversing posterior and yielding mean=.4 at x=2. These are finite declared likelihoods, not a Gaussian regression fit or evidence that extrapolation always has this spread.

Predict and recall transfer: Predict which slope gains weight after y=1; recall mean at x=3 is 2.4 and variance 1.44 under the original posterior.

Required observable evidence: Expose both lines and probability weights, with mean distinct from candidate lines.

Source obligation: [Rasmussen–Williams author textbook, chapter2](https://gaussianprocess.org/gpml/chapters/RW2.pdf), acquired body, §2.1 and eq2.5 posterior normalization. This finite two-slope likelihood is locally declared, not the book Gaussian example; latent/observation uncertainty decomposition follows the explicit independent local construction.
